html:
The railway across Canada from Montreal to the Pacific coast, built by the Canadian Pacific Railway company from 1881 and completed in November 1885, when the last spike was driven at Craigellachie in British Columbia.

Building it was a promise. British Columbia joined Canada in 1871 on the condition that a railway would link it to the east within ten years. The project nearly broke the government of John A. Macdonald in a bribery scandal and nearly bankrupted the company. Under the American manager William Van Horne, crews pushed across the prairies, the rocky shield north of Lake Superior and the Rocky Mountains. In British Columbia thousands of Chinese workers did the most dangerous work, and many died.

The line moved troops west to crush Louis Riel's North-West Rebellion in 1885, which helped win more money for it. It then brought settlers to the prairies and carried their wheat east, binding the country together. Like the US transcontinental railroad, it also cut through the lands of First Nations peoples.
sum: The railway across Canada from Montreal to the Pacific coast, built by the Canadian Pacific Railway company from 1881 and completed in November 1885, when the last spike was driven at Craigellachie in British Columbia.
